candidates.title: [3.14] gh-160324: Keep `io.StringIO` state after `MemoryError` (GH-160325)
candidates.body:
Allocate before consuming the accumulated writes in realize() and
make_intermediate(), and reset the size when the contents are lost,
so that later calls do not index outside the internal buffer.

Shrink the buffer of the accumulating writer before finishing it, so
that getvalue(), read() and the other methods leave the contents
unchanged when they fail with MemoryError instead of dropping them.

candidates.title: gh-149584: `_remote_debugging`: Read stack chunks directly instead of through the page cache
candidates.body:
`process_single_stack_chunk` would read the chunk with `_Py_RemoteDebug_ReadRemoteMemory` instead of going through the page cache. Reading chunks through the page cache doesn't really do anything:

 * on Linux pages are 4KB, so it goes straight to `process_vm_readv`
 * on macOS the chunk is exactly one page, the sampler keeps its own cache and nothing else in the sample reads that page, so all the paged read adds is a retry after the first `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS`

That retry can only succeed after the target has mapped a new chunk at the same address, so the sampler ends up parsing a chunk that is not the one the thread state pointed at. `Invalid stack chunk size 0` is the symptom (a live chunk never has size 0):

```bash
maurycy@gimel cpython-rd-base (main 312222f) % sudo dtrace -q -Z -x dynvarsize=64m -n '
  pid$target:_remote_debugging*:copy_stack_chunks:entry { self->in_copy = 1; self->fails = 0; }
  pid$target:_remote_debugging*:copy_stack_chunks:return /self->in_copy/ { @per_copy[self->fails] = count(); self->in_copy = 0; }
  pid$target::mach_vm_read_overwrite:entry /self->in_copy/ { self->addr = arg1; }
  pid$target::mach_vm_read_overwrite:return /self->in_copy && self->addr/ { @kr[arg1] = count(); self->fails += arg1 != 0; self->addr = 0; }
  END { printa("  chunk read kr=%d: %@d\n", @kr); printa("  copies with %d failed reads: %@d\n", @per_copy); }' \
  -c "./python.exe repro_chunk_retry.py 5000"
  chunk read kr=1: 954
  chunk read kr=0: 10607
  copies with 2 failed reads: 315
  copies with 1 failed reads: 324
  copies with 0 failed reads: 4361
```

324 copies got `KERN_INVALID_ADDRESS` and then a successful read of the same address a few microseconds later.

`deep_recursion` oracle target at 100kHz, `cache_frames=True`, 3s:

| error | main | direct chunk read |
|---|---|---|
| chunk read failed (`size 16384`, `kern_return_t 1`) | 41575 | 35592 |
| frame read failed (`size 88`, `kern_return_t 1`) | 24037 | 37221 |
| Incomplete sample: did not reach base frame | 8659 | 7027 |
| Invalid stack chunk size 0 | 669 | 17 |
| total failed samples | 74940 (25.0%) | 79857 (26.6%) |

On Linux `perf stat` counts the same number of `process_vm_readv` calls with both builds.  The retried reads are reported as the original read failure now, so the error rate goes up on Oracle.

Not newsworthy IMO. I don't know how to create a not racy test here.

Context: I've found this one while reviving https://github.com/maurycy/cpython/pull/3 and investigating some Oracle numbers when aliasing.

<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

candidates.title: gh-160386: Apply changes from importlib_metadata 10.0 and document the shared protocols
candidates.body:
Applies importlib_metadata 10.0 and documents the protocols it adds.

## Sync

`Lib/importlib/metadata/` picks up importlib_metadata 10.0
(python/importlib_metadata#505, for python/importlib_metadata#486):
`IDistribution` and `IPackagePath` protocols in `_meta.py`, both
`@runtime_checkable`, exported from `importlib.metadata`. The `compat` and
`_compat` packages, which hold `localize` and the warning it raises for a
provider's incomplete `Distribution` subclass, are excluded from the port as
usual, so only the protocols arrive here.

## Documentation (gh-123976)

- Documents `IDistribution` and `IPackagePath`.
- Corrects the `PackageMetadata` entry, which described itself as "a concrete
  implementation of the PackageMetadata protocol" and linked to the backport's
  docs for the protocol. `importlib.metadata._meta.PackageMetadata` is itself a
  `Protocol`, and is exported in `__all__`.
- Links to the backport's new
  [Caveats](https://importlib-metadata.readthedocs.io/en/latest/caveats.html)
  page from the overview's `seealso`, from `IDistribution`, and from the custom
  provider example.

The caveats themselves — the two class hierarchies, what the backport
substitutes and what it passes through unchanged, and what that asks of
consumers and of custom providers — now live in the backport's documentation
(python/importlib_metadata@be2ea93bc), the concern being largely the backport's
rather than the stdlib's.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)


<!-- gh-issue-number: gh-160386 -->
* Issue: gh-160386
<!-- /gh-issue-number -->

auto_merge.commit_message:
Apply the changes from importlib_metadata 10.0, which introduces the
``IDistribution`` and ``IPackagePath`` protocols, and document them.

A custom provider's objects reach consumers of both ``importlib.metadata``
and the ``importlib_metadata`` backport, whose concrete classes are
unrelated to each other, so neither library's ``Distribution`` or
``PackagePath`` describes what a consumer actually receives. The protocols
name that interface instead, and both libraries present them.

* Add ``IDistribution`` and ``IPackagePath``, and annotate
  ``distribution()``, ``distributions()``, ``files()``,
  ``Distribution.files``, ``EntryPoint.dist`` and ``PackagePath.dist``
  with them.
* Document both protocols, and point consumers and custom providers at the
  backport's caveats page for the consequences of the split hierarchies.
* Correct the ``PackageMetadata`` entry, which called it a concrete
  implementation of a protocol defined in the backport when it is itself
  that protocol.
* Test that the objects handed to consumers satisfy the published
  protocols.

Closes gh-123976.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
